observation.visible_scene: Indoor rug-cleaning bay. A beige shaggy rug lies flat on a white tarp marked with brown stains. A worker wearing tall white rubber boots stands at the far edge holding a long-handled wand (head labeled 'PROTIMA'). A blue blower/fan bearing the 'MOUNTAIN RUG CLEANING' logo sits at the upper right. A bright white highlight streak (reflection on the wet foreground tarp) persists throughout.
visible_changes: At t=0 the dragging is already underway: a thick brown foam/dirty-water mass sits on the rug's center-left beneath the wand head.

The wand head is pulled leftward and then toward the camera, dragging the brown mass across the rug surface; the mass elongates and deforms (translation plus spreading), not merely translating rigidly.
Around the mid-to-late frames the brown mass reaches the rug's front-left edge and breaks apart into a turbulent brown water stream that flows toward the camera over the foreground tarp.

After the mass leaves the rug, the wand is lifted and hovers above the front-left corner; the left strip of the rug now looks wetter/flatter while the right strip stays dry-shaggy and largely unchanged.
The worker's boots shift slightly in stance as the wand is moved.

The background (fan, tarp stains, rug outline) keeps its position, indicating the camera is essentially static; the wand head appears to grow larger because it moves closer to the lens, not because of a zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the brown dirt/foam was applied to the rug before t=0 (process already ongoing at the first frame).
What becomes of the drained dirty water and whether the rug is fully cleaned afterward.
The operator's upper body, hands, and the wand's handle grip (out of frame).
uncertain_details: Exact tool function (squeegee vs. extraction wand) is not confirmable from the frames.
Whether the left rug strip is actually cleaner or merely wet/flattened is ambiguous.
Any very slight camera tilt and the precise timing of the boot step are uncertain.
